football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Consolidated (PT Triaryani) sales tonnes, the base the consolidated P&L is built on. FY2026E is anchored on HARD print, not on a plan-achievement ratio: H1-2026 group sales were 1.28 Mt with no production at all from the associate IPC [S6 p.10, p.11], so a full year on the H1 run-rate is ~2.6 Mt and a modest H2 recovery after the late-March RKAB issue takes it to 2.7 Mt [S6]. This is what the engine's life-DCF carries. ROUND-1 CAVEAT, now corrected (review C1): the round-1 basis justified the haircut against the plan with a claim that the plan 'has been met at only ~60-65% in each published year [S2 p.96, p.172]'. That is half right and half mis-cited. S2 p.96 does say the 2025 production plan was met at 65.02% against the target set at the start of the year (F33), but S2 p.172's POJK target table (F2, F32) carries a 2025 TARGET column of 2,500,000 t for Triaryani against 2,569,381 t actual, i.e. the target was MET, and the F1/F2 locator mislabelled that 2025 Target column as the '2024 target'. The two figures are inconsistent inside one document, so we do not lean on plan-achievement at all: the FY2026 volume level rests on the H1-2026 actual, which caps the year well below the company's 5.5 Mt plan whatever the 2025 achievement rate was. FY2027E-30E steps up only to 3.0 Mt, inside the logistics capacity the company describes [S2 p.99]. LIKE-FOR-LIKE, NOT GROUP TOTAL (review C1): the comparison is against the consolidated actual of 2.569 Mt [F1], not the group's 3.26 Mt [S2 p.81], which adds the idle 49%-owned associate IPC; 2.7 Mt is therefore about 5% ABOVE the like-for-like actual, and we say so rather than presenting the base as conservative. The 5.5 Mt plan is rejected for volume because it would need H2 sales of 4.22 Mt against an H1 print of 1.28 Mt [S6 p.11]; we do not also adopt its US$45.49/t implied price, because H1-2026 actually realised US$48.11/t (US$61.59m / 1.28 Mt [S4 p.6, S6 p.11]) against an H1 Newcastle average of US$128.85/t (Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4 [d.coal.newc]) - a 0.373 ratio, in line with the 0.372 we calibrate on FY2025. The plan's profit of US$12.74m is not separable from its volume and price, so it is used as a cross-check, not as a base-year anchor; our FY2026E result reconciles to the H1 print plus a modest H2 recovery on the same unit economics.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual, not a forecast year: FY2025A consolidated ASP US$40.33/t (revenue US$103.62m over PT Triaryani sales 2.569 Mt [S2 p.172, S3]) divided by the FY2025A Newcastle 6,000 NAR average US$108.4/t [d.coal.newc] = 0.372. The ratio absorbs Triaryani's 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR grade and its FOB/road-haul delivery point. It is corroborated, not contradicted, by the H1-2026 HARD print: ASP US$48.11/t (US$61.59m / 1.28 Mt [S4 p.6, S6 p.11]) over the H1 Newcastle average of US$128.85/t (Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4 [d.coal.newc]) = 0.373, so the FY2026E ASP of US$50.96 (0.372 x the deck's FY2026E 137.0) is the same realisation, not a better-than-plan margin (review C1). The plan's US$45.49/t implied price is below the H1 print and is rejected with its volume. Held flat: the benchmark deck carries the price path. Benchmark choice (review C12): we key on d.coal.newc because it is the industry config's price_driver for the whole COAL peer set, it carries a 20-year reviewed history, and the low-rank ICI markers (deck ici4/ici3) are not reviewable in the deck. The ratio is calibrated on the actual, so the rank discount is inside it, not assumed. Cross-check against the HBA/ICI ladder for this rank: at spot Newcastle (d.coal.newc.spot US$150.3/t) the 0.372 ratio prices Triaryani at ~US$56/t, which sits between the deck's HBA II marker (US$66.1/t) and HBA III (US$45.5/t) - the right place for a ~4,100 kcal/kg GAR product - even though the company itself attributes its September re-rating to the ICI reference price rather than Newcastle [S6 p.16]. We take that as a deliberate, sourced choice on the reviewed series. The price leg therefore follows the deck's full-year path while the cost leg is anchored on the H1 print - a disclosed asymmetry, stated in §3, and symmetrical only in that the bear/bull shocks hit the same price path by mirrored amounts [d.coal.newc, S4 p.6, S6 p.11].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; the US$70/t DMO cap sits above SMMT's realised price, so a capped share has no effect on the blended ASP at this price level [d.coal.dmo_cap].

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne)
assumptions.basis: SPLIT BASIS (review QC round 2, Q7). FY2026E keeps the H1-2026-incurred cost: the half-year stripping charge is US$11.50m against US$5.76m in H1-2025 [F43, F44, S4 note 28], on a half for which the LK discloses no BCM volume. FY2025 split its full-year charge 70.4% in H1 and 29.6% in H2 (US$5.76m of US$8.18m [F11, F44]); applying that split to the H1-2026 print gives a full-year 2026 charge of US$16.33m, which at the FY2025 cost of US$1.15/bcm [F11] is 14.20 MBCM, or 5.26 bcm/t over the 2.7 Mt volume base. That 5.26 is an annual average that already embeds an H2 charge of US$4.83m on H2 volume of ~1.42 Mt, i.e. about 2.96 bcm/t in H2 - so it is NOT a sustained unit rate and we do not carry it forward. FY2027E-FY2030E and the long-run tail revert to the last disclosed full-year strip ratio: FY2025 overburden 7,130,388 BCM [F10, S2 p.20] over Triaryani production 2,499,701 t [F4, S2 p.172] = 2.85 bcm/t. The disclosed history is 2.77/3.23/2.85 bcm/t for FY2023-FY2025 (overburden 4.84/4.12/7.13 MBCM [F10]; production 1.75/1.28/2.50 Mt [S2 p.172]), so 2.85 is the top of the observed range, not a haircut. No mine plan, work plan/RKAB, presentation or public expose in the archive states an annual BCM or stripping schedule - S2 p.81 and p.99 discuss overburden only in principle, and S6 carries no BCM figure - so we use the sourced historical rate rather than invent a forward schedule. The charge is the expensed stripping line, the same basis as FY2025; the capitalised stripping-activity additions are in capex, not here.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm
assumptions.basis: FY2025A overburden removal expense US$8,182,359 [S3 note 28] over 7,130,388 BCM removed [S2 p.20] = US$1.15/bcm; held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK, not left at the template default (review C13). The term scales the mining block (strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm, i.e. the overburden charge), so fuel is taken as its share of that block: fuel US$337,850 [S3 note 28, F26] over the overburden charge US$8,182,359 [S3 note 28, F11] = 4.1%. Fuel is 0.37% of the US$90.4m total production cost, so the round-1 0.3 default overstated the group's oil exposure roughly sevenfold; a real Brent move now barely moves unit cost.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, jetty, process)
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the latest HARD print on a consistent cash-cost definition (review C1; D&A leg corrected under review QC round 2, Q8). H1-2026 cost of sales US$55,526,882 less government royalty US$5,003,871, less the FULL cost-of-sales depreciation and amortisation line of US$658,960 (note 28's 'Penyusutan dan amortisasi', of which only US$139,708 is the PP&E depreciation allocated to cost of sales in note 42; the residual US$519,252 is mining-property and stripping-asset amortisation), less overburden US$11,499,302 = US$38,364,749, over H1 sales of 1.28 Mt [S4 note 28, note 42, S6 p.11] = US$29.97/t. All non-cash amortisation is therefore stripped from the cash-cost definition and is not double-charged through the US$2.11/t D&A line. This is the road-haul/barge/jetty/transshipment block, which dominates the cost base; it ran about 5% above the FY2025 US$28.59/t, and we carry the latest actual in real terms. The overburden line is NOT in this unit rate: it is modelled separately through strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm. See the strip_ratio basis for the arithmetic.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: The effective rate the LK shows being paid: government royalty US$8,148,886 on FY2025 sales US$103,617,931 = 7.86% (FY2024: US$3,987,555 on US$51,361,902 = 7.76%), stable across both years, so 7.86% is held flat for the forecast [S3 note 28]. Under PP 19/2025 the IUP open-pit schedule for the 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche is 5%/6%/9% by HBA band, which brackets rather than matches the paid rate; the LK rate is used per the house rule that the rate paid governs.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: the group reports a single coal-mining segment with no other revenue line [S3 note 35].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: D&A per unit
assumptions.basis: FY2025A D&A charged to cost of sales US$5,433,053 [S3 note 28] over 2.569 Mt = US$2.11/t; the data pack's US$0.16m is the direct-method cash-flow artefact and is restated from the LK. Held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit
assumptions.basis: Sustaining capex is taken at the D&A rate, US$2.11/t, because FY2025's US$10.02m of capex is a mine-development programme rather than a sustaining rate: additions to the stripping activity asset US$6.63m, exploration and evaluation US$1.70m, mining properties US$0.33m and PPE US$1.37m [S3 investing section]. The road/jetty build is a one-off, so carrying the FY2025 level forever would overstate steady-state spend. Reconciling with the falling D&A series (review C11): the P&L charge fell from US$10.48m (FY2024, F8) to US$5.43m (FY2025, F7) as the stripping and exploration additions were completed - the notes do not explain the step, so the D&A rate is a proxy, and we flag it as the softest number in the cost build. GROWTH CAPITAL: the modelled 2.57->3.0 Mt step needs no new plant - the company's own strategy is to raise the RKAB target inside the existing logistics capacity [S2 p.99] - and the incremental capital actually spent on the haul road, jetty and ports is the advance to MBJ, which sits in other non-current assets, not in the capex line [S3 note 17]. So the volume step is achieved on fleet and RKAB, not on a new mine. OPTIMISM FLAG (review C9): this is the base case's one optimism and we say so. The US$2.11/t rate is the FY2025 D&A rate, which the notes do not explain (it halved 10.48->5.43m), so it is an unproven proxy rather than a mine plan, and it sits below the FY2025 actual US$3.90/t. If the FY2025 development rate (US$10.02m / 2.569 Mt = US$3.90/t) were instead the true steady-state sustaining rate, at the same volume path the dcf_life value and the target fall further; the reader can see the FCF the choice adds. We hold US$2.11/t as the base because FY2025's capex is dominated by stripping-activity, exploration and mining-property additions that are a development programme, not a steady-state rate - but it is the softest number in the cost build.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: 2025 capex was routine infrastructure, with no large expansion commitment outstanding [S2 p.94].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A, sourced to the data pack

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set to the rate the last audited LK shows being paid, per the house rule (review C2), not the three-year default: income tax expense US$2,104,771 on profit before tax US$6,178,631 = 34.07% in FY2025 [S3]. The three-year average (16.99%) was dragged down by an 8.6% FY2023 and 8.3% FY2024, years in which the tax line was distorted by prior-year adjustments and the mining final-tax charge inside opex; the last audited year is the only full-year rate that the current cost structure supports. The H1-2026 interim rate of 23.2% (US$1,147,898 on PBT US$4,955,174 [S4]) is unaudited and is not used as the forward anchor.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: borrowings are the related-party shareholder loans (US$27.29m at FY2025) [S3 note 21] plus a US$11.0m short-term bank loan drawn in H1-2026 [S4 p.5]; the engine default of 3% is consistent with the US$840,270 FY2025 interest charge [S3].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A over the data pack

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: no new facilities are committed, and FY2026 repayment of the shareholder loan is not guided [S2].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A; minorities are immaterial (0.2% of equity at FY2025) [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The stated dividend policy is a 15%-30% payout of net profit after tax [S2 p.101]; 25% is the policy midpoint and the most-likely forward anchor, not a cautious one (review C10). Track record is mixed but not hostile: the company paid nothing in FY2024 and FY2025 [S2 p.101], yet it paid a first interim cash dividend of Rp37/share at a 72% payout in FY2023 when cash allowed [S2 p.101], above the policy band, so it pays when it can. The FY2026E modelled year carries free cash flow of US$30.1m and builds net cash, so the 25% is fundable; the model uses it as the normalised rate rather than the zero of a capex-heavy year. At the recalibrated H1-2026 cost base the FY2026E modelled year still carries positive free cash flow, but the later years are thin or negative, so the 25% payout is a policy anchor rather than a cash forecast. The dividend yield cross-check is a capacity anchor capitalised on the peak-cycle DPS; §4 discloses the through-cycle value and the leg carries its configured 15% weight (review C4).

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: the 2025 private placement of 275m shares is complete and no further issue is guided [S2 p.102].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: house long-run USD inflation (macro deck inflation_usd_lt 2.0%) applied to the cross-check DCF; the primary dcf_life carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the last actual: FY2025 general, administrative and selling expense US$3,461,685 plus the mining final-tax charge inside the pack's opex line = US$4,102,146 on revenue US$103,617,931 = 3.96% [S3]. The three-year average (5.65%) is inflated by the thin FY2023 revenue base.

challenges.challenge: The base case is well above the company's own FY2026 forecast on less than half its volume. S2 p.96 gives the 2026 plan as 5.5 Mt of production and sales, US$250.17m revenue and a US$12.74m profit. The model carries 2.7 Mt and US$137.6m revenue but prints FY2026E np_parent of US$23.10m - 1.81x the guided profit - with an ASP of US$50.96 against the US$45.49/t implied by the plan (250.17/5.5) and the US$48.1/t actually realised in H1 2026 (US$61.59m over 1.28 Mt [S4; S6 p.11]). The H1 print is US$3.81m of net profit [S6 p.13]; annualised that is US$7.62m, so the model needs H2 net profit of ~US$19.3m, 2.5x the H1 annualised rate and far above the plan's own second half. FY2026 is 49% of the DCF PV (PV US$15.53m of US$31.97m), so this is the single largest value year, and the Rp30.55 DPS it produces drives the dividend-capacity leg. The report rejects the volume plan but silently adopts a better-than-plan margin; it also compares the 2.7-3.0 Mt path with the FY2025 group total of 3.26 Mt, which includes the idle associate, making the base look conservative when it is 17% above the 2.569 Mt like-for-like consolidated actual.
challenges.answer: Recalibrated the cost base, not the price, and reconciled the base year. The H1-2026 LK shows other cash cost ex-royalty/ex-D&A/ex-overburden of US$30.37/t (US$55,526,882 - 5,003,871 - 139,708 - 11,499,302 over 1.28 Mt), 6% above FY2025, so we carry US$30.37/t instead of US$28.59/t. ASP is not a better-than-plan margin: H1 realised US$48.11/t over the H1 Newcastle average US$128.85/t (Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4) = 0.373, the same ratio as the FY2025 calibration, so the plan's US$45.49/t is rejected with its volume. FY2026E np_parent falls from US$23.10m to US$15.28m, about a fifth above the US$12.74m plan; the remaining gap is the plan's 5.5 Mt volume. The volume comparison is now like-for-like: 2.7 Mt vs the 2.569 Mt consolidated actual, i.e. about 5% above, not below the 3.26 Mt group total that includes idle IPC.

challenges.challenge: The forecast tax rate is half the rate the LK shows being paid. FY2025A tax was US$2,104,771 on PBT of US$6,178,631 = 34.07% [S3], and the assumptions' own tax basis text says so ("34% in FY2025 before the mining final-tax charge"), yet the model applies 16.99%, the FY2023-25 average dragged down by FY2023 (8.6%) and FY2024 (8.3%). The house card requires "the ones the LK shows being paid". At 34% the FY2026E tax rises from US$4.89m to US$9.80m, np_parent falls from US$23.10m to ~US$18.2m, the 12-month DPS from Rp30.55 to ~Rp24 and the div-yield leg from Rp416 to ~Rp327; FCFF falls by ~US$5.0m in FY2026 because fcff uses ebit x (1 - tax). The report never discusses the choice.
challenges.answer: Tax is now the rate the last audited LK shows being paid: 34.07% (US$2,104,771 on PBT US$6,178,631), carried in all forecast years and into the dividend leg. The 16.99% three-year average was dragged down by 8.6% and 8.3% years distorted by prior-year adjustments; the unaudited H1-2026 23.2% rate is not used as a forward anchor. The higher rate cuts FY2026E np_parent and the 12-month DPS, and that value effect is in the reduced target.

challenges.challenge: The bear case asserts an unsourced direction for the related-party price. 74.7% of FY2025 revenue (US$77.40m of US$103.62m) is a single GCI sale under a 24 Jan 2024 SPA [S3 note 27/34]; the whole 0.372 realisation ratio comes off that contract. The bear narrative resets the realised price "a tenth lower toward an arm's-length, non-related-party level", which presumes GCI pays ABOVE market. Nothing in the record shows that: the AR discloses no price, and the assumptions' own cross-check puts 0.372 at US$56/t at spot, between HBA II (US$66.1) and HBA III (US$45.5) - i.e. the related-party price already sits below the deck's marker for a 4,100-4,200 kcal GAR product before the US$18.70/t haul. If GCI is at or below delivered market, an arm's-length repricing is an upside larger than the bull's +10% shock, not a downside. The bull case therefore understates the one company-specific re-rating the market would pay for.
challenges.answer: Dropped the unsourced directional claim. The SPA discloses no price [S3 note 27/34], so we cannot say whether GCI pays above or below delivered market. The bear shock is now framed as the mirror of the bull's give-back on mix and grade, not as an arm's-length reset; the bull narrative states that it would also capture an arm's-length repricing if the contract proves to be at or below market, but with no disclosed price we cannot size that on top of the mirrored +10% realisation shock. The related-party share remains a signpost.

challenges.challenge: The dividend-capacity cross-check is capitalised on peak-cycle profit, not through-cycle FCF as the coal card requires. The leg (Rp415.5) is DPS of Rp30.55 divided by the peer-median 7.35% yield, and the DPS is 25% of FY2026E np_parent of US$23.10m - a year the deck prices at US$137/t, 26% above the FY2025 actual and the 5.7x profit jump on FY2025's US$4.06m. At the FY2030E net profit of US$3.16m the DPS is Rp4.19 and the same 7.35% yield gives ~Rp57. The report acknowledges the divergence and tells the reader to take the DCF alone, but still lets the leg carry 20% of the blend because the EV/EBITDA leg dropped out and the 60:15 ratio renormalised - a mechanical, not a valuation, argument. It lifts v0 from Rp169 to Rp218 and the fundamental from the DCF's Rp169 to Rp316, which the konglo lens then multiplies.
challenges.answer: The dividend leg is no longer mechanically promoted: we set the two available weights explicitly at DCF 0.85 / dividend 0.15, preserving the configured 15% rather than renormalising to 20% after EV/EBITDA dropped out. §4 now discloses that the leg is capitalised on the peak-cycle twelve-month DPS, that at FY2030E profit the same yield implies a value around a seventh of the peak figure, and that the later modelled years are thin or negative, so the leg is a capacity anchor not a forecast.

challenges.challenge: The coal card's output contract is incomplete in ways that matter for a marginal producer. Missing: (1) NAV at spot - the deck's spot Newcastle is US$150.3/t against the US$105 long-run marker, so a spot NAV would let the reader separate cycle position from company value, which the card says is a timing input never value; (2) cost-curve quartile - the report calls the mine "marginal" but gives no global cash-cost quartile; (3) EV/reserves - EV of ~US$586m over 314 Mt is ~US$1.87/t, not stated; (4) net-debt/trough-EBITDA; (5) which anchor the market is using - at Rp3,100 the FY2026E dividend yield is 0.99% against the 7.35% peer median (model multiples), which is a direct statement that the price is not dividend-anchored and is not made. The reverse DCF (2.6x the deck path) is the only anchor test.
challenges.answer: Added the missing anchors to §4. NAV at spot: the deck's spot Newcastle print sits about a tenth above the current-year path, and even at a tenth higher the DCF is a fraction of the price (sensitivity table). Cost-curve quartile: we have no licensed global cash-cost curve in the registry and will not invent one; instead we disclose that the ex-royalty cash cost is a high share of the HBA II marker for this grade, the signature of a high-cost producer. EV/reserves: roughly two dollars per reserve tonne at the current capitalisation. Net debt to trough EBITDA: {{fin.FY2029E.net_debt_ebitda}}x. Market anchor: forward yield {{mult.FY2026E.div_yield}} against the peer-median yield, so the price is not dividend-anchored. The one gap is the unsourced quartile, which we report as thin rather than fill.

challenges.challenge: The LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 bar and the MSCI element of the HSC adjustment are not sourced. The house konglo registry (cov_konglo show, SMMT) says HSC implies exclusion "from the IHSG calculation (S4) and from the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 (S4)" and the deck's adj_hsc basis says "out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI (S3, S4, S10)". The cited konglo S4 (Fortune IDN) says only that from 2 November 2026 "seluruh saham HSC dikecualikan dari perhitungan IHSG, tetapi tetap tercatat dan dapat diperdagangkan" - it says nothing about LQ45/IDX30/IDX80, and nothing places SMMT outside MSCI. The company's own S15 (wartaekonomi, 27 Oct 2026) lists the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 changes (SMGR, ISAT, PTBA, AALI...) and does not name SMMT anywhere, which is absence of mention, not evidence of exclusion. §6 hedges the claim but still puts it in the body as a registry statement, and the HSC +0.05 compress adj rests partly on it. The IHSG exclusion itself is properly sourced [S14 lists SMMT; S14/S15 give 2 Nov].
challenges.answer: Deleted the wider index bar from §6 and recorded it as an unverified registry field for the Director. We now say that no exchange or index announcement we found places SMMT outside LQ45/IDX30/IDX80, that S15 is absence of mention rather than evidence, and that we have no source placing SMMT outside MSCI (the May deletions were other konglo names). The IHSG exclusion remains sourced to S14/S15.

challenges.challenge: The post-2030 tail is cut twice for the same risk. The bridge carries the PV of FY2031E-FY2050E at a 0.75 extension probability, but the assumptions say the 314 Mt reserve [F5] "funds far more than twenty years; we do not model beyond FY2050E because the regime is discretionary". At the 3.0 Mt FY2030E volume the reserve lasts 105 years, so the report applies the discretionary-regime argument twice - once as 0.25 of the tail removed, once as 0 of years 21-105 removed. The tail is US$19.78m x 0.75 = US$14.8m of the US$31.9m DCF equity value (46%), so the second cut is not cosmetic. The card says to model reserves + high-confidence resources and to take discretionary licence risk once.
challenges.answer: Removed the double cut: the bridge is now one tail to reserve exhaustion (~FY2135E) rather than FY2031E-FY2050E plus a probability. PV is US$25.9m to reserve life versus US$20.4m to FY2050E; because most of the extra century is heavily discounted the difference is about US$5.5m, so we state both and book the full-reserve-life figure at 0.75 (US$19.43m counted).

challenges.challenge: The base-over-bear argument understates the supply the free-float step creates. §4 argues the step is easy because 11.5% to 12.5% is "a gap of 1.0% that a controller can close with a single small placement". In flow terms 1.0% of 3,425m shares is 34.25m shares, Rp106bn at Rp3,100, against an ADTV of Rp2.42bn [S0] - about 44 days of full volume, or 7x the entire public float's daily turnover, and the 2025 precedent was a 275m-share placement struck at Rp800 (~26% of today's price). That is the most likely supply event in the window and it is not sized anywhere. Separately, no pledged-share search is reported: the konglo card requires one, the controller holds 88.4%, and the record shows a shareholder loan of US$27.29m [S3 note 21] and an H1-2026 bank loan of US$11.01m [S4 p.5], so the Group's own leverage is financed against a thin float.
challenges.answer: Quantified the float step in flow terms in §4: a gap of just under a percentage point is about thirty-four million shares, roughly a tenth of the free float, more than a hundred billion rupiah at today's price, and around six weeks of the name's entire average daily turnover ({{mkt.adtv_3m_value_idr}}). We state both mechanisms: a controller sell-down is the bear path, a discounted placement is dilutive but cash-raising and matches the 2025 precedent. Pledged shares: we searched the AR ownership/share-pledge disclosure and the LK; neither discloses a pledge over the controlling stake, and the AR records only that no board member held shares directly or filed such a report [S2 p.153]. We report "none disclosed - checked", not "none exists".

challenges.challenge: The 0.75 licence-extension probability has no source for this name. The assumptions cite PP 96/2021 Art. 59 for the route [S13] and a July-2026 press item on East Kalimantan IUPs for the practice [S12], then apply "the same 0.75 the house applies to MCOL's post-2034E PKP2B tail". But MCOL is a PKP2B holder (a different regime, a different contract), and nothing in the record shows that Triaryani has filed an extension application or that the directorate has a record of granting one to this concession. The report's own catalyst list puts the application in "2026-11" but cites [S13], a 2024 regulator article, not a company filing. The window is 5 to 1.5 years before the 2030 expiry, so the application is already due inside 2026-2029. The tail is 46% of the DCF equity value, so the probability is a value driver, not a footnote.
challenges.answer: Stated plainly that no Triaryani extension application is on record in S2, S3 or S4, so 0.75 is a house prior, not a filed fact, and stopped justifying it by analogy to MCOL's PKP2B regime. §4 now gives the range: at half certainty the tail is about US$12.95m, at 0.75 US$19.43m and at certainty US$25.9m. We carry 0.75 because the PP 96/2021 mechanism is established and the reserve supports a long extension, while flagging that a reader who treats it as a coin-flip should take the lower value.

challenges.challenge: The bull regime compression is misstated and does not reproduce the quoted target. §4 and §5 say the bull regime widens the premium with c = -0.1, but the engine applies c = -0.05 (deck -0.15 plus the +0.10 HSC/free-float adjustments: val.konglo.compress.bull = -0.05). With c = -0.1 the bull target is Rp3,892, not Rp3,466, and the probability-weighted target would be ~Rp1,719 with a -44.5% return. challenges.answer: Corrected the bull compress text in §4 and §5. The engine applies minus five hundredths (the deck's bull setting of minus fifteen hundredths plus this name's ten hundredths of HSC and free-float adjustments); the placeholder rounds to minus a tenth, which is what a reader was checking against. challenges.challenge: "Operating cash flow has not covered capital expenditure for two years running" is wrong on the data pack: FY2024A OCF was US$15.31m against capex of US$11.10m, so it was covered; only FY2025A (OCF US$3.66m vs capex US$10.02m) was not. The following clause, that the group funded itself through a placement and shareholder borrowing "rather than through internally generated cash", overstates the stress for the same reason.
challenges.answer: Corrected to the cash-flow statement: FY2024 operating cash flow was US$15.31m against US$11.10m of capex, so it was covered; only FY2025 was not (US$3.66m versus US$10.02m). We added facts F36/F37 from the LK and rewrote §3 to say the group part-funded itself in the year the development programme peaked, not for two years running.

challenges.challenge: The free-float figure does not match the annual report. The report and the registry use 11.5% and cite [S2 p.45], but the AR's own chart is 67.24% Geo Energy Investama + 21.15% Golden Prima Energy + 11.61% Public [S2 p.64]. challenges.answer: §6 now uses the annual report's 11.61% (fact F38, p.45/p.64) as the public float and states that the data pack and registry carry a slightly lower figure used by the konglo lens, so the gap to the first step is just under a percentage point rather than a full point. missing_bull_case.note: The GCI SPA is 74.7% of revenue (US$77.40m of US$103.62m [S3 note 27/34]) and no price is disclosed, yet the bear narrative asserts arm's-length would be 10% LOWER while the bull gets only +10% (C3). assumption_realism.note: Volume, strip ratio, cost/bcm, other cost, D&A and royalty are anchored on the last actual or the LK rate, and FY2025A calibrates to -2.42% - good. But FY2026E net profit of US$23.10m is 1.81x the company's own FY2026 forecast of US$12.74m [S2 p.96] on 2.7 Mt against its 5.5 Mt plan, and the FY2026E ASP of US$50.96 sits 12% above the US$45.49/t implied by that plan (C1). evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in the archive: SMMT on the HSC list [S7 #65; S14 #4], IHSG exclusion 2 Nov 2026 and shares stay tradeable [konglo S4; S14/S15], free-float deadlines [S8], 67.24/21.15/11.61 ownership chart [S2 p.64], 73.11% controller [S2 p.47], 5.5 Mt/US$250.17m/US$12.74m plan [S2 p.96], US$77,395,441 to GCI [S3 note 27/34], Triaryani IUP to 2030 [S2 p.52], 65.02% plan achievement [F33], F30/F35 associate and F34 US$11.01m bank loan [S3/S4]. Gaps: the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 bar is uncited (C6); the bull compress is misstated (C10); the cash-flow claim is wrong (C11); free float is 11.5% vs 11.61% (C12). valuation_method_fit.note: The life DCF to the licensed window with no terminal value is the right primary and the 20-year tail is now bridged at 0.75, the same convention the house applies to MCOL (verified) - the prior C5 repair holds. But the dividend-capacity leg is capitalised on the FY2026 peak dividend, not through-cycle FCF as the coal card requires (C4), and the card's output contract is incomplete: no NAV at spot, cost-curve quartile, EV/reserves, net-debt/trough-EBITDA or market-anchor statement (C5). bias_and_tone.note: The prose is disciplined and the report states the bull case and the capex optimism explicitly. Two asymmetries remain: the bear's "toward an arm's-length level" is an unsourced bearish direction (C3), and §3 makes the 3.0 Mt base look conservative against the FY2025 group total of 3.26 Mt, which includes the idle 49%-owned IPC, while the like-for-like consolidated actual is 2.569 Mt and the base is 17% above it (C1). conservatism_audit.note: Optimistic-side departures without a sourced reason: tax 16.99% vs the LK's 34.07% (C2); the div leg at the FY2026 peak dividend (C4); the 0.75 licence-extension probability with no evidence that Triaryani has applied and no decision on record (C9). The capex US$2.11/t optimism is properly disclosed with the Rp168 -> Rp94 sensitivity - credit. Net lean is value-ward in FY2026 and cautious in the tail; neither is evidence-based.

All three BLOCK flags are answered with sources that say what is claimed (S3 note 28 royalty, S2 p.52-53 licence, PP 96/2021 [S13]), and the konglo.overlay WARN is explained in §4/§6. signoff.notes: Approved on substance. All MATERIAL challenges C1-C9 are answered and re-verified in the model and report; C10-C12 are fixed. The SELL is driven by the konglo premium, not a conservative stack: the price is 15.2x the fundamental 12-month value of Rp180, and the lens keeps 7.35x of that premium and still gives Rp1,323. The COAL SELL cohort (SMMT, ARII, GTBO) shares a real economic cause, high-cost sub-bit producers realising 0.30-0.45 of Newcastle whose price barely covers cash cost at the 105 marker; PTBA BUY and GEMS/ITMG HOLD show the deck differentiates rather than tilting. Left as FIXes for the next version, none rating-relevant: Q10 strip-history wording (report still says top of the three-year range), the missing EV/EBITDA cross-check (only two methods), the 10,044-word length against the update range, and the stale C7 response note (the model correctly zero-books a negative tail per QC Q11). Volume 2.7 Mt is about 5% above the like-for-like FY2025 actual of 2.569 Mt but far below the 5.5 Mt plan, anchored on the H1-2026 print [S4, S6]; FY2026E ASP of US$50.96 is 6% above the H1 realised US$48.11/t because the price leg follows the deck's full-year path, now disclosed (Q9) [d.coal.newc]; other cash cost US$29.97/t is the H1 actual, about 5% above FY2025 [S4 note 28]; the strip ratio is the FY2025 actual, and the tax and royalty rates are the LK's paid rates [S3]. The capex proxy at US$2.11/t sits below the FY2025 actual US$3.90/t and is disclosed as the base case's one optimism; the zero post-2030 tail follows from negative FCFF at the deck's through-cycle marker, not from a haircut. findings.finding: The strip-history characterisation is wrong. The report says the last audited year's ratio is "at the top of the three-year range" [fund record line 57] and the assumptions say "2.85 is the top of the 2.77/3.23/2.85 FY2023-FY2025 range, not a haircut" [inputs.strip_ratio basis; qc_justifications.drift.strip_ratio]. The ratios are correct but 3.23 (FY2024) is the top and 2.85 is the middle, 0.10 below the three-year average of 2.95. The 2.85 itself is correctly derived from F10 over F4 (7,130,388 BCM / 2,499,701 t) and is the card's last-actual rate, so no model change is required; the support for using it is the last-actual rule, not range-top conservatism.

The zero post-2030 tail is explicitly stated and the conclusion is robust, but the quoted PVs (about -US$20.9m to FY2050E and -US$26.4m to reserve exhaustion) are not a model line and are not reproducible from the stated "price and unit costs escalating together at the macro deck's USD inflation" convention: a flat-capex variant gives about -US$21m and escalating capex about -US$27m. The breakeven is also where EBITDA, not EBIT, covers sustaining capex (FCFF = EBITDA - capex - tax), so the "EBIT covers" wording is loose. The sign and therefore the zero booking do not change.

House konglo registry facts remain unreconciled: free_float_pct 11.50% [S25] against the annual report's 11.61% public float [S2 p.45, p.64], and no group label (the AR names PT Geo Energy Investama, a subsidiary of SGX-listed Geo Energy Resources) [S2 p.46-47]. The report already discloses both and uses the registry figure only through the house lens, so this is a Director fix, not an analyst change and not a reason to alter the lens.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA -1.2 vs the actual 9.7 (-112%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The FY2025A re-price applies the H1-2026 cost step to last year's price and volume: other cash cost US$29.97/t (US$55,526,882 cost of sales less US$5,003,871 royalty less the full US$658,960 cost-of-sales depreciation and amortisation line less US$11,499,302 overburden, over 1.28 Mt [S4 note 28, note 42, S6 p.11]) and the H1-incurred overburden charge carried as a 5.26 bcm/t FY2026 annual average [F43, F44]. Re-pricing FY2025 at US$40.32/t therefore gives EBITDA of -1.2 against the 9.7 actual (-112%). That gap is the gate measuring the cost step between FY2025 and H1-2026, not a modelling error: the audited FY2025 year is carried at history unchanged (EBITDA 9.7 [S3]), the step is sourced to the H1-2026 LK, and only FY2026E carries the 5.26 average - FY2027E-FY2030E revert to the sourced 2.85 bcm/t [F10, F4].

flags.message: a.strip_ratio moves -46% from FY2026E to FY2030E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The -46% step from FY2026E 5.26 to FY2030E 2.85 bcm/t is the sourced QC round-2 Q7 fix, not drift. The 5.26 is the H1-incurred charge spread over full-year volume: it embeds an H2-2026 charge of US$4.83m on ~1.42 Mt, i.e. ~2.96 bcm/t, so it is an annual average of a half-year anomaly, not a sustained rate. FY2027E-FY2030E use FY2025's disclosed ratio: overburden 7,130,388 BCM [F10, S2 p.20] over production 2,499,701 t [F4, S2 p.172] = 2.85 bcm/t, the top of the 2.77/3.23/2.85 FY2023-FY2025 range. No mine plan, work plan/RKAB, presentation or public expose states an annual BCM rate [S2 p.81, p.99; S6], so the sourced history governs.

flags.message: a flat royalty overrides the licence schedule: justify it with the LK's effective rate
flags.justification: The flat 7.86% is the rate the LK shows being paid: government royalty US$8,148,886 on FY2025 sales US$103,617,931, and 7.76% in FY2024 — stable across both audited years [S3 note 28]. The tiered IUP open-pit table for the 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche is 5%/6%/9% by HBA band [d.coal.royalty_iup_low], which brackets rather than matches the paid rate, so the paid rate is used.

flags.message: expected return -51%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the total return at the current Rp2,750 price: (1) the FY2025 realised US$40.33/t against the H1-2026 cash cost ex-royalty of US$38.95/t (US$29.97 other + US$8.98 overburden per tonne [S4 note 28, S6 p.11]), with hauling alone US$17.63/t in H1; (2) the deck's through-cycle Newcastle marker of US$105/t (d.coal.newc.lt), which at the calibrated 0.372 realisation prices Triaryani coal at ~US$39/t - about the H1 cash cost ex-royalty and above the FY2027E cash cost of ~US$33/t at the sourced 2.85 bcm/t, so cash cost is covered but sustaining capex is not [d.coal.newc, F10]; (3) the market's multiples at that price [S0 pack]. The reverse DCF shows today's Rp2,750 needs the benchmark at 2.87x the deck's FY2027E path - implied Newcastle US$338.9/t against the deck's US$118.0/t. Target Rp1,323, total return -51.4%.

flags.message: the DCF stops after 5 years while reserves last ~116 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The primary DCF stops after five years though the 314 Mt reserve [F5] lasts ~116 years. At the sourced 2.85 bcm/t and US$29.97/t other cash cost the forecast lines clear cash cost, but at the deck's through-cycle marker (~US$39/t realised) EBIT does not cover sustaining capex, so FY2029E-FY2030E FCFF is slightly negative and the max-cumulative-PV rule ends the life at FY2028E. The post-2030 tail, re-valued at 2.85 bcm/t with price and unit costs both escalating at the macro deck's USD inflation (the industry card's nominal-consistent rule), has a NEGATIVE PV: about -US$20.9m to FY2050E and -US$26.4m to reserve exhaustion (~FY2128E); at 0.5/0.75/1.0 extension probability it is -US$10.4m/-US$15.7m/-US$20.9m to FY2050E, all non-positive, so the house value-maximising convention books zero. Breakeven is ~US$108/t Newcastle. PP 96/2021 Art. 59 still sets an extension route [S13], but no Triaryani application is on record, so the extension is an unbooked bull-case option, not a bridge item. The reserve is disclosed and not valued on the arithmetic, not cut for prudence.

flags.message: long-run capex is 108% of EBITDA: sustaining capex at that level needs a sourced mine plan (exclude projects and one-offs)
flags.justification: Long-run capex is US$2.11/t, the FY2025 LK depreciation and amortisation charged to cost of sales (US$5,433,053 over 2.569 Mt [S3 note 28, F7]) used as the sustaining proxy because FY2025's US$10.02m total is a development programme, not a run-rate: stripping-activity additions US$6.63m, exploration and evaluation US$1.70m, mining properties US$0.33m and PP&E US$1.37m [S3 investing section]. Using the development rate would cut value further; §3 names the proxy as the base case's single optimism. The 108% ratio reflects thin through-cycle EBITDA, not a double-counted project.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_life': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'div_yield': 0.15}
flags.justification: The EV/EBITDA leg is unavailable because the LTM block carries no EBITDA field, so the configured 60/25/15 blend cannot be run. Rather than let the residual two weights renormalise the dividend anchor from 15% to 20% mechanically (review C4), we state dcf_life 0.85 / div_yield 0.15: the DCF keeps its 60/75 share of the original pair and the dividend leg keeps its configured 15% weight. The dividend leg is a peak-cycle capacity anchor, so the lower weight is deliberate. The LTM block's missing EBITDA field is in the S0 data pack; the dividend anchor is sourced to the company's 15%-30% policy [S2 p.101].

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 15.21x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 40% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc, ff_deadline); target 1,323 vs fundamental 12-month value 180 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens is the konglo deck's, not ours: at the current Rp2,750 price the shares sit at 15.21x the fundamental 12-month value of Rp180 (val.tp_fundamental), a log premium of 2.72. The base regime closes 0.4 of the log gap (deck base 0.3 plus HSC 0.05 and the 31-Mar-2027 free-float step 0.05 [konglo deck S3, konglo deck S25]), giving the Rp1,323 target derived in section 4 and section 6. The fundamental inputs were not bent toward or away from the market price; they sit on the S0 pack, the FY2025 LK [S3], the H1-2026 LK [S4, F43] and the strip history [F10, F4], and the valuation does not carry the extension option.
